query: Which Australian city founded in 1838 contains a boarding school opened by a Prime Minister of Australia and named after a school in London of the same name.

pipeline_result.response: The Australian capital city is Canberra, which was founded on 26 July 1901 as a new town with the name "Aus-Town" (now known as Canberra). The building that houses the Australian National University and the Australian National Museum were originally named after the Prime Minister of Australia, Sir John A. Macquarie, who served from 1824 to 1836.
